module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# *abc* conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abc_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace ABC

/--
The radical of `n` denoted is the product of the distinct prime factors of `n`.
-/
def radical (n : ℕ) : ℕ := n.primeFactors.prod id

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem radical_16 : radical 16 = 2 := by
  have : Nat.primeFactors 16 = {2} := by
    rw [show 16 = 2 ^ 4 by decide, Nat.primeFactors_pow]
    · norm_num
    · decide
  norm_num [radical, this]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem radical_17 : radical 17 = 17 := by
  rw [radical, Nat.Prime.primeFactors (by norm_num), Finset.prod_singleton, id]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem radical_12 : radical 12 = 6 := by
  rw [radical, show 12 = 2^2 * 3 by rfl, Nat.primeFactors_mul (by norm_num)
    (by norm_num), Nat.primeFactors_pow _ (by norm_num),
    Nat.Prime.primeFactors (by norm_num), Nat.Prime.primeFactors (by norm_num)]
  rfl

/--
Quality `q(a, b, c)` of the triple `(a, b, c)` is defined as `q(a,b,c) = log (c) / log (rad(abc))`.
-/
noncomputable def quality (a b c : ℕ) : ℝ := (c : ℝ).log / (radical <| a * b * c : ℝ).log

/--
For every positive real number `ε`, there exist only finitely many triples `(a, b, c)` of coprime positive integers, with `a + b = c`, such that `c > rad(abc)^(1+ε)`
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem abc (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    {(a, b, c) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ ({a, b, c} : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧
    a + b = c ∧ (radical <| a * b * c : ℝ)^(1 + ε) < c}.Finite := by
  sorry

/--
For every positive real number ε, there exists a constant `K_ε` such that for all triples (a, b, c) of coprime positive integers, with a + b = c we have `c < K_ε rad(abc)^(1+ε)`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem abc.variants.lt_constant_mul (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ K,
    ∀ (a b c : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → 0 < c → ({a, b, c} : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime → a + b = c →
    c < K * (radical <| a * b * c : ℝ)^(1 + ε) := by
  sorry

/--
For every positive real number ε, there exist only finitely many triples `(a, b, c)` of coprime positive integers with `a + b = c` such that `q(a, b, c) > 1 + ε`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem abc.variants.quality (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    {(a, b, c) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ ({a, b, c} : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧
    a + b = c ∧ quality a b c > (1 + ε)}.Finite := by
  sorry

end ABC

reformulations.difference: Coprimality is encoded using `({a, b, c} : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime`, which checks distinct values rather than distinct positions in the triple.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under positivity and `a + b = c`, we have `a < c`. Set-pairwise coprimality therefore implies `Nat.Coprime a c`, equivalently `Nat.Coprime a b`. Conversely, coprimality of a and b implies coprimality of all three pairs. Repeated values introduce no extra triples: a = b forces a = b = 1. This agrees with Wikipedia's coprimality note. The full statement's equivalence to the gcd(a,b) = 1 formulation was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The uniform-bound formulation uses the same set-based encoding of coprimality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the stated positivity and sum hypotheses, the set-based condition is equivalent to `Nat.Coprime a b`, so the quantified uniform bound is unchanged. Additionally, applying the bound to (1,1,2) forces K > 0; an explicit positivity requirement would not strengthen the statement. The full equivalence to a formulation with gcd(a,b) = 1 and an explicitly positive real constant was proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The finite-quality formulation also expresses coprimality through a set of the triple's values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Positivity and `a + b = c` make set-pairwise coprimality equivalent to gcd(a,b) = 1, including the repeated-value case. Hence the set whose finiteness is asserted is exactly the source's set of exceptional triples. The full statement equivalence was proved in Lean.

review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. The radical definition and all three numerical tests are correct. Although radical(0) = 1 and quality has totalized logarithm/division values, the conjecture hypotheses exclude these problematic inputs: rad(abc) > 1 for every admissible triple. Lean also verifies the equivalence of the quality and power inequalities, and that (1,8,9) is an exceptional triple for ε = 1/5. Wikipedia's formulations match all three conjectures, and its statement that no proof has gained broad acceptance supports the research-open tags. Checks are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, which compiles without errors or warnings; the full statement-equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx.
